title: Create Subnets With for_each
scenario: Create subnets from a map with for_each so adding a subnet is just a map entry.
constraints: Use for_each over a map variable.

focus.title: Complete the aws_subnet block
focus.todo: Use for_each over the subnet map and reference each.key/value.

hints.why: for_each creates one instance per stable key. Adding or removing an entry changes only that instance, whereas an index-based list can shift every later instance when the order changes.
hints.what: Complete the marked region in `main.tf`. The work is inside `resource "aws_subnet" "this"`. Use for_each over the subnet map and reference each.key/value. Use the visible constraints as the checklist for names, values and references before you run the tests.
hints.when: Use for_each when each instance has a durable identity, usually from a map or a set of strings. Use count for identical instances where position is the identity.
hints.how: Open `main.tf` and work only inside `resource "aws_subnet" "this"`. Use this code shape: cidr_block; vpc_id; for_each; availability_zone. Use the already-declared references instead of hardcoded values: `each.value`, `var.vpc_id`, `var.subnets`, `each.key`. Keep the block header and braces, indent nested blocks by two spaces, and add one argument or nested block at a time. Run the tests after each small change so the first failure points at the next name to fix.
